verify-309.summary: Verified #309 against scripts/roadmap/ at main HEAD (post-#307/#308). Repo guard passed (mvox-app.git). Issue #309 confirmed zero comments, contract quoted in full. All six requested areas checked with file:line evidence below.

Per #309's contract ('The link wraps the card's own number and title — in every case') the fix is to wrap exactly these two spans (or their combined text) in one `` replacing the two bare spans, leaving labels/lead outside. Sub-issues nest at line 218: `const subIssuesHtml = childrenHtml ? `

Lead insertion point: #309 wants lead 'under the title and above the labels' — that is precisely between line 222 (title span) and line 223 (labels span); today there is nothing there, so a `${escapeHtml(lead)}` (only when non-empty, no placeholder) slots in at that seam. findings.claim: (2) fetch-issues.ts interfaces at HEAD — GitHubIssue/RoadmapIssue shapes, html_url NOT carried, normalizeIssue keeps, fixture gaps
findings.evidence: fetch-issues.ts:40-54: `interface GitHubLabel { name?: string; color?: string; }` and `interface GitHubIssue { number; title; state; state_reason?; labels; body; pull_request?; closed_at?; }` — no `html_url` field declared anywhere in GitHubIssue. render.ts:32-50: `RoadmapLabel { name: string; color: string | null }` and `RoadmapIssue { number; title; state; stateReason; labels; body; closedAt; subIssues? }` — no `htmlUrl`/`html_url` field. Confirmed via `grep -rn html_url scripts/roadmap/` returning zero hits across .ts and fixtures. normalizeIssue (fetch-issues.ts:67-87) maps: state, stateReason (validated to 'completed'|'not_planned'|null), labels (name+color, filtered empty-name), body verbatim, closedAt (`raw.closed_at ?? null`), subIssues initialized `[]` — it does NOT read or carry `raw.html_url`, so adding the field requires: (a) `html_url: string` on GitHubIssue interface, (b) `htmlUrl: string` on RoadmapIssue interface (naming to match existing camelCase convention: closedAt/stateReason), (c) a new line in normalizeIssue's return object `htmlUrl: raw.html_url`, (d) every entry in scripts/roadmap/fixtures/live-shaped.json needs an `"htmlUrl"` key added (currently absent on all 8 fixture issues, read directly lines 1-95), (e) fetch-issues.spec.ts's normalizeIssue test inputs (e.g. lines 40-51, 58-71, 73-83, 88-98, 101-106, 108-133) construct raw GitHubIssue objects without html_url and assert `.toEqual(...)` on the labels-only subset so they won't break structurally, but a new dedicated spec is needed asserting `result.htmlUrl` is carried through — none exists today.

findings.claim: (3) parseFrontmatter + displayTitle — slugline handling, unknown-keys-ignored, lead slot-in point, escaping path
findings.evidence:
render.ts:52 `FRONTMATTER_RE = /^---?
([\s\S]*?)?
---(?:?
|$)/` anchors to string start so a later '---' (horizontal rule) never matches (covered by render.spec.ts:109-111). parseFrontmatter (render.ts:59-73) parses via `parseYaml`, returns the full mapping object (or null on non-mapping/malformed/absent) — unknown keys survive into the returned Record and are simply never read by displayTitle, which is the 'ignored' mechanism (no allowlist/filter step exists; render.spec.ts:92-98 confirms 'ignores unknown keys' by asserting only that slugline is still read out). displayTitle (render.ts:79-84) is the ONLY consumer of parseFrontmatter's output today: `const slugline = frontmatter?.slugline; if (typeof slugline === 'string' && slugline.length > 0) return slugline; return issue.title;` — a second function `displayLead(issue): string | null` mirroring this exact pattern (`const lead = frontmatter?.lead; return typeof lead === 'string' && lead.length > 0 ? lead : null;`) is the natural slot-in, called once per renderIssue alongside displayTitle. Escaping path for authored strings: title/slugline go through `escapeHtml()` (render.ts:143-145, escapes only `&<>`, deliberately leaves quotes alone per the comment at 132-136) at the point of HTML emission — render.ts:222 `${escapeHtml(title)}`. A lead field must go through the identical `escapeHtml(lead)` call at its insertion point (between lines 222-223) to match #309's 'Escaped like every other authored string' checkbox and the existing XSS-safety tests pattern (render.spec.ts:537-543 'escapes HTML in sluglines too').

findings.claim: (4) CSS/inline-style situation — card styles, closed-dim opacity interaction with a link, underline/colour needs
findings.evidence: render.ts:298-308 inline `<style>` block. Relevant rules: `.issue { display: block; border: 1px solid #ccc; border-radius: 0.5rem; padding: 0.75rem; margin: 0.5rem 0; }` (line 300), `.issue[data-state="closed"] { opacity: 0.6; }` (line 301 — this dims the WHOLE article including any descendant link, since opacity is inherited/composited on the subtree, not overridden per-child), `.issue-number { color: #666; margin-right: 0.5rem; }` (302), `.issue-title { font-weight: 600; }` (303, no color rule — inherits body's default link-less black text; since it's currently a span not an <a>, no default link styling applies at all). No `a` selector exists anywhere in the stylesheet today (confirmed via grep — zero matches for `<a ` or CSS `a {` in render.ts). Consequence for #309's checkbox 'visibly a link at rest': turning the number+title spans into an `<a>` wrapping them will, by default browser UA styles, render blue+underlined text UNLESS overridden — but since the existing `.issue-number`/`.issue-title` classes set explicit `color`/no-color rules, those inline styles override the UA default color (browsers apply author CSS over UA defaults for color), so the link would likely render in the same #666/black as today with no visible affordance unless a new rule like `.issue-title-link { text-decoration: underline; }` or similar is added targeting the new anchor. The closed-card opacity (0.6) applies uniformly to the link along with everything else in the card — no special-case is needed structurally, but a real check: at 0.6 opacity a link's underline/color must still pass contrast against the page background; nothing in the current stylesheet computes or tests that, so it is a design decision for whoever implements, not something existing code already handles.

findings.claim: (5) Specs to flip or extend — card-structure assertions, fixture updates, escaping-spec pattern
findings.evidence: render.spec.ts assertions that currently assert (and would need extending, not necessarily breaking) title-in-textContent rather than a specific link element: line 172-179 `for (const i of liveShaped) { const el = entry(doc, i.number); expect(el.textContent).toContain(i.title); expect(el.textContent).toContain(String(i.number)); }` — this passes either way (textContent survives wrapping in ) but does not assert the exists, so a NEW test is needed asserting e.g. `entry(doc, n).querySelector('a')?.getAttribute('href')` equals the fixture's htmlUrl, and that the 's accessible text is exactly `#N `. render.spec.ts:564-571 and board.spec.ts:104-105/130-134/217-219 assert nesting via CSS descendant selectors (`doc.querySelector('[data-issue="289"] [data-issue="290"]')`) — these remain valid regardless of an added <a> since data-issue stays on the <article>, not moved onto the <a>. cli.spec.ts:44,46 assert `html.toContain('data-issue="305"')` and title text — safe under the change. Fixture updates needed: scripts/roadmap/fixtures/live-shaped.json (all 8 entries, lines 1-95) needs an `htmlUrl` key added to each object for any test that exercises the real fixture end-to-end (render.spec.ts's `liveShaped` usages throughout, and cli.spec.ts's integration run at lines 20-21/39-47 which reads this exact file) — without it, a spec asserting the anchor's href against the fixture would have nothing to assert against (undefined/missing). Escaping-spec pattern to mirror for lead: render.spec.ts:537-543 `it('escapes HTML in sluglines too', ...)` builds an issue with `body: '--- slugline: <img src=x onerror=alert(1)> --- '` and asserts `html).not.toContain('<img src=x')` — a directly analogous `it('escapes HTML in lead too', ...)` using `lead: <script>...` in frontmatter is the pattern to add, plus a 'no lead → no placeholder, no empty element, no height change' test mirroring render.spec.ts:197-200 ('renders an issue with no labels at all without crashing').

findings.claim: (6) Baseline suite count + accessible-name situation with <a> wrapping #N+title
findings.evidence: `pnpm vitest run scripts/roadmap` at main HEAD: `Test Files 6 passed (6)`, `Tests 100 passed (100)`, ~5-6s duration, zero failures — clean baseline before #309 work starts. Accessible-name check: `grep -n "aria-label" scripts/roadmap/render.ts scripts/roadmap/*.spec.ts` returns zero matches — no aria-label exists anywhere in render.ts or any spec today, and no code path in renderIssue/renderLabel/renderBoard constructs one. So wrapping #N+title in a plain `#N Title` with no aria-label gives the link its accessible name from content alone, exactly as #309 requires ('Content-derived, never a templated aria-label') — there is nothing at HEAD that would inject a conflicting aria-label; this is a from-scratch addition, not a fix to an existing violation.
